title: Polynomial versus power-series coefficients in a formal monoid completion
statement:
Let $L$ be a field or a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], let $\mathfrak m_L$ be its maximal ideal ($0$ for a field, $pL$ for a Cohen ring with uniformizer $p$), let $P$ be a fine saturated sharp additive monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $n\ge0$. Here sharp means that $0$ is the only invertible element. Put $D=L[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and $\mathfrak m_D=\mathfrak m_LD+(T_1,\ldots,T_n)D$. For any coefficient ring $V$, $V[P]$ is the finite-sum ring with basis $z^q$, $q\in P$, and product $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. Set $E=L[P][T_1,\ldots,T_n]$, $\mathfrak a=(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q
e0),T_1,\ldots,T_n)E$ and $\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak m_D,z^q\ (q
e0))D[P]$. The natural inclusion $E	o D[P]$, sending $c,z^q,T_i$ to the same coefficient, monomial and variable, induces for every $j\ge1$ an isomorphism of rings $E/\mathfrak a^j\xrightarrow{\sim}D[P]/\mathfrak b^j$. These isomorphisms commute with reduction from $j+1$ to $j$. Consequently they induce a continuous isomorphism of complete local $L$-algebras $\Psi:B=\varprojlim_j E/\mathfrak a^j\xrightarrow{\sim}H=\varprojlim_j D[P]/\mathfrak b^j$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It fixes every $z^q$ and $T_i$, carries $N_B=(z^q:q
e0)B$ onto $N_H=(z^q:q
e0)H$, and the induced identification $B/N_B\cong H/N_H\cong D$ fixes $L$ and all $T_i$. The truncations and completion comparison include the trivial monoid and the empty list of variables.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, interpretation of the displayed formal monoid models; agent-supplied comparison, extracted from old completed-chart Step 3. The separate task is to identify the finite quotients of polynomial versus power-series coefficient rings and their compatible inverse limits, including the monomial quotient. It does not restate the dimension or normality theorem.

proof.text:
By [lem-trf-sharp-fs-orthant-embedding], identify $P$ with a submonoid of $\mathbf N^r$ inside $\mathbf Z^r$; the sum of coordinates is strictly positive on nonzero elements. Apply [lem-trf-positive-monoid-adic-filtration] to this embedding and write $
u(q)$ for its finite maximum decomposition length. Also apply it to $Q=P	imes\mathbf N^n\subset\mathbf Z^{r+n}$, with the sum-of-coordinates weight. Its decomposition length at $(q,e)$ is $
u(q)+|e|$: split $(q,0)$ into a longest decomposition and $(0,e)$ into $|e|$ coordinate generators for the lower bound; in any decomposition at most $
u(q)$ terms have nonzero $P$ component and at most $|e|$ remaining terms have a nonzero variable component. Under $E=L[Q]$, its combined ideal is exactly $\mathfrak a$. Hence for a polynomial $F=\sum_{q,e}c_{q,e}z^qT^e$,
$$F\in\mathfrak a^j\ \Longleftrightarrow\ c_{q,e}\in\mathfrak m_L^{\max(j-
u(q)-|e|,0)}\quad\hbox{for every }(q,e).$$

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied finite-quotient comparison of the displayed formal monoid models.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-positive-monoid-adic-filtration] with coefficient ring $D$, ideal $\mathfrak m_D$, and monoid $P$. For a finite sum $G=\sum_q f_q(T)z^q\in D[P]$, it gives
$$G\in\mathfrak b^j\ \Longleftrightarrow\ f_q\in\mathfrak m_D^{\max(j-\nu(q),0)}\quad\hbox{for every }q.$$
For a positive exponent $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients], applied over $L$ with $J=\mathfrak m_L$, says precisely that $f_q\in\mathfrak m_D^k$ iff its coefficient at each $e$ of degree $|e|<k$ belongs to $\mathfrak m_L^{k-|e|}$. For $k=0$ there is no restriction. Thus the criterion for $G\in\mathfrak b^j$ is the coefficient criterion of Step 1, now allowing power-series coefficients. In particular $E\cap\mathfrak b^j=\mathfrak a^j$, so the natural map $E/\mathfrak a^j\to D[P]/\mathfrak b^j$ is well-defined and injective.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied finite-quotient comparison of the displayed formal monoid models.

proof.text: Given $G=\sum_{q\in S}f_q(T)z^q$ with finite $S$, replace every $f_q$ by its polynomial truncation $f_q^{<j}=\sum_{|e|<j}c_{q,e}T^e$. This is a polynomial since there are finitely many variables. The omitted series has zero coefficients below degree $j$, so [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] puts it in $\mathfrak m_D^j$. Therefore $G-\sum_{q\in S}f_q^{<j}z^q\in\mathfrak b^j$. This proves surjectivity and hence the required ring isomorphism $e_j$. Each $e_j$ is induced by the same inclusion $E\to D[P]$; reducing a representative from level $j+1$ to $j$ therefore gives the same class in either order.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied finite-quotient comparison of the displayed formal monoid models.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-adic-inverse-limit-iso], the compatible $e_j$ induce a ring isomorphism $\Psi:B\to H$, whose $j$th component is $e_j$ applied to the $j$th component of its input. It is an $L$-algebra map and fixes $z^q$ and $T_i$, since this is true at every level. The inverse has components $e_j^{-1}$, so both maps preserve the kernels of level projections. They are therefore continuous for the inverse-limit adic topologies.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied finite-quotient comparison of the displayed formal monoid models.

proof.text: For completeness in the ideal-adic sense, choose a finite list of nonzero generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ of $P$, deleting any zero generators. Every nonzero $q$ is $g_i+q'$ for some $i$ and $q'\in P$; thus $(z^q:q\ne0)$ is generated by the $z^{g_i}$. Consequently $\mathfrak a$ and $\mathfrak b$ are finitely generated: use these monomials, the $T_i$, and $p$ in the Cohen case. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] to each ring as a module over itself. Its conclusion gives completeness and identifies each level-projection kernel with the corresponding extended ideal power. In a commutative completion ring this module-generated ideal power equals the power of the extended ideal, by expanding products of generators. Thus the topologies in Step 4 are also the topologies of these extended ideals.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied finite-quotient comparison of the displayed formal monoid models.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $D$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring, complete and separated for $\mathfrak m_D$. Together with the lattice embedding and positive weight of Step 1, these are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-formal-monoid-residue-domain] with coefficient ring $D$ and monoid $P$. It gives that $H$ is local and that its constant-$P$-coefficient homomorphism $c_H:H\to D$ is surjective with kernel $N_H$, and is a $D$-algebra map. Since $\Psi$ fixes each monomial and is surjective, it carries the ideal generated by those monomials, $N_B$, onto $N_H$. Hence $B$ is local as well, and $c_H\Psi$ induces $B/N_B\cong H/N_H\cong D$. This identification fixes $L$ and every $T_i$: their images under $\Psi$ are the same coefficient elements in $H$, on which $c_H$ is the identity.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied finite-quotient comparison of the displayed formal monoid models.

proof.text: All constructions allow $P=\{0\}$: take the empty monoid generating list, $\nu(0)=0$, and $N_B=N_H=0$. For $n=0$, the only variable exponent is $e=0$, the truncation in Step 3 retains each coefficient, and $D=L$. These conventions also apply when both are trivial; no step assumes a positive monoid rank or a nonempty variable list.
